On Friday night, Artyom was the last one to leave the office.
He didn't know he wouldn't get out until Monday.
Between the seventh and eighth floors, the elevator jerked and stopped.
He pressed the emergency button.
Nothing.
No signal.
A metal box inside a concrete shaft blocks almost everything.
Battery, 3%.
He shouted for help.
Only silence answered.
His first thought was to force the doors open and climb out.
That's the most dangerous mistake you can make.
Most elevator injuries happen not inside the cabin, but when people try to escape on their own.
And the elevator won't fall.
It hangs on several steel cables.
If they snap, safety brakes lock it inside the shaft.
He took a deep breath and told himself not to panic.
The building wouldn't open until Monday.
Half a bottle of water, one chocolate bar.
He switched his phone to airplane mode and turned it off to save the last few percent.
Screaming non-stop wastes energy and water.
So he decided to knock.
Three knocks, every 15 minutes.
No answer.
Without food, a person can last for weeks.
Without water, about three days.
He took one sip every few hours.
On Saturday night, he knocked again, like always.
And for the first time, someone answered.
Three knocks.
From above.
He almost laughed.
Someone was in the building.
Someone would get him out.
They pulled him out on Monday morning.
He asked the guard who had been knocking in the shaft.
The guard just frowned.
The building had been empty all weekend.
The cameras showed no one.
And no one gets into that shaft without a key.
So who answered him?
